title: Four-state engagement histories and component estimates
footnotes: CI, confidence interval; RR, risk ratio; ADL, activities of daily living; ELSA, English Longitudinal Study of Ageing; HRS, Health and Retirement Study; KLoSA, Korean Longitudinal Study of Ageing; SHARE, Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe. Absent at both interviews is the four-state reference. Component estimates compare stopping with no stopping.
methods: Four-state engagement histories distinguish continued participation, stopping, starting, and absence at both interviews. The reference category was absence at both interviews. Separate stopped-versus-continued models included only participants engaged at the first interview. The component models included stopping drinking, regular physical activity, and paid work together, with current status included for each activity. Pooled estimates required at least three evaluable cohorts. Drinking and paid-work four-state death models had only two evaluable cohorts, so cohort estimates are shown.

footnotes: B0: age, sex, interview wave. B1: B0 + self-rated health. B2: B1 + activities of daily living (ADL) limitation count (death). C, concordance statistic; CI, confidence interval; NB, net benefit; Δ, augmented minus base. Brier scores measure prediction error; calibration assesses predicted versus observed risk. Entries are cohort ranges except pooled ΔC and mean ΔNB. B1 versus B0 is the difference between pooled C statistics (CI unavailable). NB thresholds (low/middle/high): death, 2/5/10%; new ADL limitation, 5/10/20%.
methods: Prediction analyses used person-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated five times. Five hundred participant-cluster bootstrap samples held out-of-fold predictions fixed, so their uncertainty excludes variation from refitting models. Pooled changes in the C-statistic use safeguarded Hartung–Knapp intervals. The self-rated-health increment is the difference between the separately pooled C statistics for B1 and B0; a paired confidence interval is unavailable. The table gives the range of cohort-specific base and augmented C-statistics, Brier scores, and calibration intercepts and slopes. Brier scores measure prediction error; calibration intercepts and slopes assess agreement between predicted and observed risk. Net-benefit changes are simple cohort means at the stated thresholds.

B0 included age, sex, and interview wave. B1 added self-rated health, and B2 added activities-of-daily-living limitation count for death. Count means the number of activities stopped. Two-point history included status at both interviews for each everyday activity and was compared with current engagement at the second interview. The complete-health sample required recorded self-rated health, plus recorded activities-of-daily-living limitation count for death. All paired comparisons used the same person-intervals within each outcome. B0 rows show baseline values.

footnotes: All estimates compare two or more activities stopped with none. CI, confidence interval; RR, risk ratio; ADL, activities of daily living; IADL, instrumental activities of daily living; ELSA, English Longitudinal Study of Ageing; HRS, Health and Retirement Study; SHARE, Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe.
methods: Current-status-held models included the status of all everyday activities at the second interview and were compared with models without those status terms on the same person-intervals. The number of activities initially present, current status, and the number stopped are linked by construction. Some combinations cannot occur, so these conditional associations rely on model restrictions across structurally unobserved combinations. They do not identify a within-status comparison supported at every number of activities stopped.

Concurrent-health models added recorded changes between the first and second interviews. Each estimate is paired with the unconditional model fitted on the same sample. The joint model used the health measures available in that cohort. Frailty-index-dependent rows come from the original analysis. The original constructor used 32 candidate deficits and required at least 26 observed deficits, dividing the deficit sum by the number observed and requiring information from all three deficit groups. This definition follows the recorded constructor audit.

methods: Paid-work exit comparisons distinguished retirement-linked status from other exits where the source interview measured it. The direct contrast is the ratio of the other-exit risk ratio to the retirement-linked-exit risk ratio, using their within-model covariance. Both component risk ratios use continued paid work as the reference. Retirement-linked status does not establish whether an exit was planned or voluntary. The descriptive work-exit synthesis contains two cohorts and is separate from the main rule requiring at least three.

Word-recall change was analyzed by a linear model with recall at the second interview included as a covariate and participant-grouped robust variance. Recall estimates and their intervals are standardized mean differences in SD units. They are pooled from evaluable cohorts and use safeguarded Hartung–Knapp confidence and prediction intervals.
